lines.text: I know. I was there each time you lifted the mask.
lines.context: The god Anpu, walking beside the dead priest Ankhu. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried.

lines.text: A son. A father. A husband. A man who stopped speaking.
lines.context: Anpu, gentle, naming the man's grief without judgement.

lines.text: The Duat keeps what the living lose. But the road asks something first.
lines.context: Anpu, comforting first, then a quiet warning.

lines.text: Your name, at every gate. Hold it as you held it in the water.
Walk with me, Ankhu. The night is long, and the gates are many.
lines.context: Anpu at a vista over the night hills, inviting, warm, the last line of the scene.
